decisions.rationale: Long-form name of one specific disease (familial Mediterranean fever with late onset), given as the minimum necessary span.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate section 1 and section 5

decisions.rationale: The abbreviation FMF in the title parentheses is a synonymous mention of familial Mediterranean fever and is annotated as a separate mention.
Long form familial Mediterranean fever names one specific disease with no further categorization.
The abbreviation FMF in parentheses is a synonymous mention of the long form and is annotated separately.
FMF modifies the noun attack in first FMF attack, so it functions as a modifier rather than a standalone disease mention.
FMF modifies the noun clinic in FMF clinic, so it functions as a modifier.
FMF modifies the noun patients in consecutive FMF patients, so it functions as a modifier.
FMF modifies the noun clinic in the FMF clinic, so it functions as a modifier.
The word disease here is a very general term and is excluded.
FMF modifies the noun gene in FMF gene, so it functions as a modifier.
Late-onset FMF names a specific form of the disease that patients had, so it is a disease mention rather than a modifier.
The word disease is a very general term referring to their disease, and is excluded.
FMF here names the disease itself as the object of manifestations (manifestations of FMF), not a modifier of another noun.
Amyloidosis refers to a family of multiple specific amyloid diseases, so it fits the Disease Class definition.
Chronic arthritis refers to a family of multiple arthritic conditions rather than one specific definition.
Myalgia is a symptom rather than a disease name, so it is outside the disease mention scope.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate section 1 (only disease mentions)

decisions.rationale: The word disease is a very general term (severity of the disease, mild disease) and is excluded.
FMF modifies the noun population in regular FMF population, so it functions as a modifier.
FMF refers to the disease itself in the onset of FMF, not as a modifier of another noun.
The word disease in a milder form of disease is a very general term and is excluded.
